newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech trade deficit narrows as exports surge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech trade deficit narrows as exports surge.

text.p: The Czech Republic's trade deficit narrowed in June to 9.6 billion crowns from 13.6 billion in the same month in 1996, the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) said on Tuesday.

The overall figures were within the range of market expectations -- a Reuters poll on Monday forecast a deficit of 10.5 billion crowns -- although exports grew far more rapidly than had been anticipated.

"I am surprised that the dynamic of export growth was so high -- 31 percent year-on-year in June -- which indicates that exports must have grown even in volume terms, not only in crown terms," said Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka.
Analysts said the trade performance had been boosted by a sharp depreciation in the crown against the dollar and mark.
Since an all-time high against its now defunct mark/dollar basket on February 10, the crown has fallen by 24 percent against the dollar and 15 percent against the German currency.
Petr Kukla of Girocredit Banka said the currency markets had received the figures calmly with some early mark selling pushing the crown up slightly to 19.14 to the mark from over 19.2 at the opening.

However, he added that the crown could be expected to weaken in coming days as the Czech National Bank (CNB) continued to trim interest rates and the effects of heavy flooding begin to filter through into new economic indicators.
"The crown may go lower because the interest rates are going lower and after these figures there are going to be no good figures to wait for," said Kukla.
Around one third of the Czech Republic has been hit by record flooding which began in the first week of July and could not have affected the June trade figures.
However, many analysts believe the floods will become a key problem for all sectors of the Czech economy as the year progresses.
Sobisek said the first economic effects of the floods on the trade situation would probably show up in July figures to be released next month.
"July export figures will be influened by the flood and the stoppage of production in some big companies," said Sobisek.
After the figures were released, the CNB, in line with its gradual policy of cutting rates, eased the one and two week repo rates to 15.7 percent from 16.0 percent.

Oto Otepka, a bond dealer at ING Barings, said that in normal circumstances he would have expected the positive trade figures to encourage the central bank to ease interest rates further but since the floods it was difficult to predict how much more the CNB would do.
"Three weeks ago I was perfectly sure that the interest rates would come down before the end of this year, even below the levels it had been in May," he said.
"But now because of the floods I'm very, very uncertain."
In a televised interview late on Monday, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus refused to answer a question on whether the flooding would push the state budget into deficit in 1997.
The central bank has said that control of inflation remains its number one policy priority. -- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
